name: One King Down
label: Equal Vision
lede: An Albany straight edge band went through three singers in five years, kept a bassist on the Equal Vision payroll, and made one six-song EP that fans still rate first. Along the way, a guitarist auditioned for the Foo Fighters.

eras.title: Albany, before the growl
eras.text: One King Down started in Albany, New York around brothers Bill and Mike Scoville, playing crunchy, metallic hardcore in the mould of Snapcase and Earth Crisis. Their first singer made one CD and was gone before anyone outside upstate New York had heard of them.

years.h: A demo cassette called Jawbreaker starts it
years.p: Brothers Bill Scoville (bass) and Mike Scoville (guitar), guitarist Matt Wood, drummer Derrick Van Wie and singer Bill Brown self-release it in Albany.

years.h: Absolve is the first CD, and Brown sings it
years.p: Trainwreck Records issues four songs, including Nine Eyes and The Killing Fields, with Paul Benedetti engineering.
years.xp: Discogs credits Brown as the voice on Absolve. Equal Vision later tacked all four songs onto the CD of Gravity Wins Again in 2000.

years.cap: Rob Fusco on stage at the Saratoga Youth Center, mid-1990s
yt: Opening for Earth Crisis, QE2, Albany, May 6, 1995
years.h: Rob Fusco takes the mic from Brown
years.p: His growl and his vegan straight edge lyrics carry the band well past Albany. Not everyone else in the band goes vegan.
years.xp: Fusco told Lambgoat in 2008 that the band was "heavily touring from '95 to '98, and from '99 to '01." Wikipedia notes the whole band was drug-free, but only some members were vegan.

eras.title: The EP people still judge them by
eras.text: Rob Fusco was out front, Bill Scoville had an inside line to Equal Vision, and the six-song Bloodlust Revenge came out of it. A tour with Hatebreed, Earth Crisis and Sick of It All followed.

years.h: Bloodlust Revenge lands on Equal Vision, where Bill Scoville works
years.p: Six songs built on Fusco's vegan straight edge lyrics, sold by the thousand through independent channels. Wikipedia says most fans still rate it the band's finest recorded hour.
years.xp: Punknews later called it a six-song hardcore opus with "nary a bad track." IDIOTEQ hears Snapcase and Earth Crisis in it, and says the lyrics take on mass drug use and a society too apathetic to help itself.

years.cap: Rob Fusco at the Saratoga Youth Center, mid-1990s
years.h: On the road with Hatebreed, Earth Crisis and Sick of It All
years.p: The tour after Bloodlust Revenge goes international and puts the band on bills with [[Vision of Disorder|618a18b1-dec3-4c4a-813b-988d9c065722]] too.

eras.title: Who's singing this week
eras.text: Internal fights pushed Fusco out right before a national tour. The band went through two replacements, split, came back with Fusco, lost its drummer and finished as a four-piece. Then it skipped Hellfest and stopped.

years.cap: Rob Fusco at the Saratoga Youth Center, mid-1990s
years.h: Fusco walks out right before the Earth Crisis tour
years.p: Internal conflict drives him out just before a national run supporting [[Earth Crisis|88a6037e-87ba-492a-a54c-c927aa620cb8]] and [[Madball|c9e0a0f5-9f53-4247-a52d-a3f29d975e17]]. Ryan Downey of Burn It Down fills in for exactly two shows.
years.xp: Downey was never meant to stay. The band looked to Syracuse and found Jon Peters, who sang on their first full-length.

years.h: A singer from Syracuse, and a first full-length
years.p: Jon Peters sings God Loves, Man Kills, EVR 48, recorded at Max Trax Studios in Albany with Paul Benedetti. Punknews said it sounded like a different band altogether.
years.xp: Around this time guitarist Mike Scoville auditioned for the [[Foo Fighters|67f66c07-6e61-4026-ade5-7e782fad3a5d]]; Wikipedia says the job went to someone else. The band also shared a split CD with Spirit of Youth on Europe's Good Life Recordings in 1998.

years.h: Peters quits, the band splits, and Fusco is back when it re-forms
years.p: After more touring Jon Peters leaves and One King Down break up for a short time.
years.xp: A Punknews reviewer heard about Fusco's return from Equal Vision's Ian early in 2000 and wrote that "I was thrilled." Fusco, he said, sang in a metal-tinged hardcore band but still sounded human.

years.h: A Clash tribute album gets an Albany hardcore band
years.p: Their version of London Calling goes on Chord Records' City Rockers: A Tribute to the Clash, next to [[Hot Water Music|c83907ee-8b5a-4547-8f68-96572243ea7f]], [[Dropkick Murphys|e8374874-4178-4869-b92e-fef6bf30dc04]] and [[Kid Dynamite|c5300096-cfb0-4801-b146-166e2d02f08a]].

years.h: Gravity Wins Again is the last Equal Vision release
years.p: EVR55, recorded at Max Trax in Albany, with [[Jacob Bannon|d5c2a3e1-a52a-4af6-8e3f-aa2c4dc69af7]] on art direction. The CD adds the four Absolve songs.
years.xp: Punknews counted only three new songs, called it "a kickass ep," and heard a new degree of intensity in Fusco's vocals.

years.h: Derrick Van Wie leaves and Matt Wood moves from guitar to drums
years.p: Van Wie is still on Gravity Wins Again. Wood takes the kit and the band carries on as a four-piece.
years.xp: Fusco told Lambgoat about riding in the van while Wood kept perfect time with a Van Halen song on the radio through a mountain tunnel, and was still in sync when the signal came back. He called Wood "one of the most astonishing musical and vocal talents I've ever had the pleasure to know."

years.h: A skipped slot at Syracuse Hellfest ends the band
years.p: Their last records are a split on When Angels Shed Their Wings Volume 2 and a three-way 7" with Mindsnare and Day of Contempt.

eras.title: Fusco's other band, and a demo nobody heard
eras.text: With One King Down done, Fusco found a second home fronting Most Precious Blood, and the old band tried once to reconvene on tape. In 2017 the EP that mattered most got its anniversary reissue.

years.h: Fusco finds a new band in Most Precious Blood
years.p: When Tom Sheehan leaves to go back to school, Most Precious Blood, formed from the remains of Indecision, take on Fusco. He fronts them on Trustkill for years.

years.h: A demo called Rob Loves, Man Kills never comes out
years.p: The band records a demo CDr whose title reworks their 1998 album around Fusco's name.

years.h: Bloodlust Revenge turns 20 and the vinyl sells out
years.p: Equal Vision reissues it remastered on vinyl, and BrooklynVegan later reports the physical copies sold out.
years.xp: Equal Vision's own description of it was "the band's finest recorded hour." A digital copy went for $5. IDIOTEQ says the stop-and-go rhythms and heavy groove can still be heard in today's metalcore.

eras.title: Kids again at This Is Hardcore
eras.text: After 17 years off, the Bloodlust line-up came back and ended up on bills with bands it once opened for.

years.cap: One King Down's drummer on stage, April 26, 2019
years.h: Seventeen years later, This Is Hardcore
years.p: Fusco, the Scoville brothers, Matt Wood and Derrick Van Wie play Philadelphia, the band's first show in 17 years.
years.xp: The band announced the show in March 2018.

q: We felt like kids again. Like someone picked us up and dropped us into 1998 one more time.
One King Down, after This Is Hardcore
years.p: Upstate Concert Hall hosts All Out War, Wisdom in Chains, Downswing and Scavengers on the bill. It's the band's first New York show in 17 years.
years.xp: After This Is Hardcore the band posted that "we're still trying to process what just happened this weekend," and that it went far beyond anything they had hoped for.

years.h: Earth Crisis hands them the Firestorm shows, then Europe
years.p: One King Down support [[Earth Crisis|88a6037e-87ba-492a-a54c-c927aa620cb8]] at Firestorm 30th anniversary shows in Brooklyn, Cambridge, Syracuse and Amityville, then tour Europe in June with Shutdown and No Turning Back.
years.xp: Fusco told Decibel in March 2023 that "there are some rumblings from the One King Down camp."

years.h: The Belasco in Los Angeles hosts One King Down
years.p: The occasion is For The Children Fest, a long way from Albany.
